- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75+), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “rebound” or “mean reversion” effect.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the 20–30 day window, suggesting it underweights recent downward momentum or fails to adjust for seasonal/structural trends.
- Forecasts often lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly after volatility spikes — model is slow to react to new information.
- Model overreacts to recent high prices, producing artificially high forecasts when prices are already near or above 75 — should dampen response to recent peaks.
- Model underestimates the impact of short-term volatility (e.g., 70–72 range) and fails to adjust forecasts downward when prices are near support levels.
- Model shows strong bias toward “smooth” trends — fails to capture sudden drops or spikes, especially when preceded by high volatility.
- Should apply a “mean reversion” correction for forecasts >75 or <70, adjusting toward historical 30-day average if deviation exceeds 2–3 standard deviations.
- Model underestimates the effect of “policy-driven” price corrections — should add a small downward bias (e.g., -0.5 to -1.5) when true price drops below 70 after a spike.
